races.title: State Senate, District 20
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Caroline Menjivar
cands.bio: California state senator for District 20 since December 2022. U.S. Marine Corps veteran (2009–2016), former EMT and social worker. Earlier worked as a field deputy for a Los Angeles councilwoman, East Valley representative for the mayor, and director of new program initiatives at MEND.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed on Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, Working Families Party, California Federation of Labor Unions, California Nurses Association, California Teachers Association, California Environmental Voters, Equality California, Sierra Club Angeles Chapter and Reproductive Freedom For All.
In 2022 she was endorsed by state senator Henry Stern, LA County Supervisor Sheila Kuehl, the San Fernando Valley Young Democrats, California Environmental Voters and the Los Angeles Times.

cands.gaps: We found no documented positions or actions from her on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay and pensions, gun laws, abortion restrictions, or school choice and teacher pay. We found no documented stance on data centers or on development beyond her opposition to SB 79. We found no reporting on controversies involving her own conduct. Her campaign website was thin and gave no policy detail. Her Ballotpedia survey describes her legislative accomplishments mostly in her own words, and these were not independently confirmed.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia says she was born in Woodland Hills, Los Angeles, and her own 2022 survey and Wikipedia say she was raised in the San Fernando Valley, where she still lives (Panorama City).

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: State Senator since December 2022 (District 20); earlier a field deputy for a Los Angeles city councilwoman and East Valley representative for the mayor; EMT, social worker with a UCLA master's degree, and Marine Corps veteran 2009–2016.
qual.why: Nearly four years of actual legislative service, including a seat on the Budget and Fiscal Review Committee, plus local government staff and social-policy work. Committee chairing was not counted.
qual.label: Nearly four years of actual legislative service, including a seat on the Budget and Fiscal Review Committee, plus local government staff and social-policy work. Committee chairing was not counted.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Voted against SB 79 in 2025, a bill allowing apartment construction near major transit hubs. She said housing should not be built near transit lines in her district that "are not going to be utilized by working class individuals."

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 1 backed by their record, 0 only promised (needs 2 to score)

roots.summary: Ballotpedia says she was born in Woodland Hills, Los Angeles, and her own 2022 survey and Wikipedia say she was raised in the San Fernando Valley, where she still lives (Panorama City).

cands.name: Tony Rodriguez
cands.bio: U.S. Army veteran (1980–2005), human resources professional and operations director. Part of the founding team of Lead Staffing (2011) and its Lead Mission Critical division. Has run for Congress (2022), Assembly (2024) and State Senate District 20 (2026). Has held no elected office.

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as endorsed by the Republican Party of California and Reform California, plus several voter-guide recommendations, for the 2026 race.

In his own 2026 survey he lists endorsements from CAGOP, LAGOP, the Los Angeles Hispanic Republican Club, Burbank GOP, the San Fernando Valley CRA and the Howard Jarvis Taxpayers Association. These are self-reported.

cands.gaps: We found no record of elected office or official actions, so there is nothing on what he has done in government. We found no statements from him on data centers, development or growth, property tax cuts, investor or foreign land buying, H-1B visas, abortion, guns, or school choice and teacher pay. His date of birth was not available. His account of his time on a state disability board comes only from his own survey answer.

local.label: Roots 90: He was born in New York City but says he was raised in Northeast Los Angeles and graduated from Franklin High School, then moved to Tujunga in 1994.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He served 25 years in the U.S. Army (1980–2005) and works as an operations director and human resources professional. He is on the founding team of Lead Staffing, a staffing company founded in 2011. He has never held elected office.
qual.why: A management and business background and a long military career put him in the middle band. He has no legislative service and no policy or budget career on record. Board and community roles are not counted.
qual.label: A management and business background and a long military career put him in the middle band. He has no legislative service and no policy or budget career on record. Board and community roles are not counted.

back-police-order.evidence: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he said complete defunding of police should never be considered and that he would always be an advocate for police.

workers-first.evidence: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey he said security at the borders can and must be given priority, while upholding constitutional protection of human rights.
